facts.statement: With an authorized Google Cloud Storage client, client.list_blobs(bucket_name, prefix=prefix) iterates existing objects matching the supplied prefix.
Select the intended object by name and use bucket.blob(object_name).download_to_filename(local_path) to obtain a local dataset file.
Read a CSV with pd.read_csv(local_path, dtype=declared_types), and verify its loaded columns, row count and value representations against the expected dataset.
CSV is a delimited text format, while Parquet is a columnar format whose reader can select columns; choose the supplied format according to the required access pattern.
Use with open(path, mode, encoding="utf-8") as f for a local text identity record, and use f.read() or f.write(text) within the block.
Import the Google Cloud Storage dependency with from google.cloud import storage and construct storage.Client() using the existing authorized runtime identity.
Import pandas as pd and apply explicit per-column conversions for the declared types, inspecting the converted values rather than accepting inference as a type guarantee.

practice.objective: Write the required imports and a Python ingestion function that uses the existing authorized runtime to list the supplied object-storage prefix, select orders-b.csv by name, download it to the supplied local path, and read it with explicit declared column types. Verify the loaded observations against the supplied expectations, write a local text identity record through an explicit file handle, and explain why CSV fits the stated access pattern and when selected-column Parquet access would fit instead.
practice.success: The function retrieves orders-b.csv rather than orders-a.csv, returns the downloaded local path and loaded table, and provides checks of the expected columns, row count, and converted value representations, including the supplied order key example '0012'. The identity record is written inside a UTF-8 open-file block. The format explanation distinguishes delimited text from columnar selected-column access without changing the supplied format arbitrarily.

The columns and row count match the supplied expectations, inspected converted values retain their declared representations, and the local identity record contains the chosen object name and local dataset path.
